question:
Simplify the following.

 (sqrt{6} times sqrt{15} - 5sqrt{10}) + 3sqrt{10}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

√6 × √15 = √90 = 3√10

Expression = (3√10 − 5√10) + 3√10

⇒ −2√10 + 3√10 = √10

**∴ The correct answer is √10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: (√6 × √15 − 5√10) + 3√10

Formula Used: √a × √b = √ab

⇒ (√(6 × 15) − 5√10) + 3√10

⇒ (√90 − 5√10) + 3√10

⇒ (√(9 × 10) − 5√10) + 3√10

⇒ (3√10 − 5√10) + 3√10

⇒ −2√10 + 3√10

⇒ (3 − 2)√10

⇒ √10

**∴ The correct answer is √10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule for Surds

For any positive real numbers a and b, the square root of their product is √a × √b = √ab.

Simplifying Radicals

A radical is in simplest form when the radicand has no perfect square factors other than 1, such as √90 = √(9 × 10) = 3√10.

Addition of Like Radicals

Only like radicals (radicals with the same index and same radicand) can be added or subtracted using the rule a√x ± b√x = (a ± b)√x.
